dimensions.assessment: Affects nonimmigrant visa applicants, international travelers, and U.S. citizens seeking consular protection overseas.
dimensions.evidence: ensuring that 80 percent of nonimmigrant visa applicants are interviewed within 3 weeks of receipt and application

dimensions.assessment: Modifies financial authorities and account transfers across Department of State programs to reduce administrative processing bottlenecks.
dimensions.evidence: The unobligated balances of each amount available from fees listed in section 7081(h)... are authorized to be transferred

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes the redirection and transfer of existing collected passport surcharges, fraud prevention fees, and unobligated fee balances without specifying new net appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: passport and immigrant visa surcharges collected in any fiscal year are authorized to be made available for the costs of providing general consular services

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Passport Act of 1920, the Immigration and Nationality Act fee provisions, and Department of State authorities regarding fund transfers.
dimensions.evidence: Section 1(b) of the Passport Act of June 4, 1920 (22 U.S.C. 214(b)), is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory authorization regarding fee usage and transfer authorities for consular operations.

missing_information: Exact dollar totals of unobligated fee balances available for transfer are not disclosed in the text.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill authorizes certain passport and visa surcharges to be used for general consular services and reducing visa wait times, aiming for a benchmark where 80 percent of nonimmigrant visa applicants are interviewed within 3 weeks.
